page.layout: One column of italic verse, with the page number and running head at the top. Below the verse, the signature "I. I. B." on the right, then "AD" at the lower right. No marginal notes; faint show-through in the right margin is ignored.

p.i: Qui Syracusias celebris arces Texit, atque diu nouis potentes Lusit artibus Italum cateruas: Nostri Dedalea manus Duranti Quàm grato variant labore chartas, Quàm mutant variis typos figuris. Prata sic variant suos colores: Flores sic variant suos odores.

Ten' Chiragra feris nocere flagris Atque audire truces iuuat querelas? Inuisis lapidosa tunde nodis Pigros articulos, manúsque ineres. Desidum, licet, otiosa ventrum Cade pondera tristibus flagellis, Qui sub Santonico cutem culullo cucullo Curant molliculam atque delicatam: Et quos Ganea, quos popina pernox Nudat lucifugos, tenebriones. Manus sanguineas preme, & nocentes, Auaras, rapidas, & impudicas Quæ tam spurca suis notant libellis, Tam turpes Veneres Cupidinesque. Istis si nequeas satis nocere, Pedes excruciet simul Podagra.

page.notes: In line 7 of the second stanza, "culullo" is struck through and "cucullo" is printed beside it; both are copied as they stand, with the struck word first. "Auaras" is printed with u for the consonant and is given as "Avaras" in the verse, but I kept the printed form in the text where the scan shows it; the spelling "Lusit" is corrected from the long-s form "Lufit". The stanza structure is inferred from indentation: the first eight lines form one stanza, the rest run on from the indented "Ten'".
